title: Tigers’ Justin Verlander announces plans to retire at the end of the 2026 MLB season
content:
After 21 seasons in MLB, Detroit Tigers starter Justin Verlander announced Wednesday afternoon that he will retire at the end of the 2026 season, wanting to cap a surefire Hall of Fame career in the city where it all began.

“This season has challenged me in ways I haven’t experienced before, both physically and mentally,” Verlander wrote in a social media post. “I’ve always believed that as long as I could compete at the level I expect of myself, I’d keep playing. I never wanted to retire because of a milestone, a number, or a date on the calendar. I wanted the game to tell me when it was time.

“Over the last several months, I’ve realized that time has come. While I’m fully committed to giving my team everything I have for the rest of this season, I’ve decided this will be my last.”

Verlander, the 2011 American League MVP, two-time World Series winner and three-time Cy Young Award winner, was also named to his 10th All-Star team Wednesday as a “Legend Pick” by MLB commissioner Rob Manfred.

The 43-year-old signed a one-year, $13 million deal with Detroit this winter, returning to the team that made him an anchor of its rotation less than two years after drafting him. After making two spot starts for the Tigers in 2005, he joined their rotation for good in 2006 and spent most of the next 12 years with them before a late August trade to the Houston Astros in 2017.

This season, the right-hander made just one start with Detroit before landing on the 60-day injured list with a left hip injury.

“It’s fitting that I get to finish where it all started — with the Detroit Tigers, the organization that drafted me and gave me my first opportunity,” Verlander wrote in the statement. “Baseball has given me more than I could have imagined. It taught me discipline, resilience, and the value of continuing to adapt and evolve. I’ve been fortunate to play with and against incredible players, for outstanding organizations, and compete in front of fans who deeply appreciate the game.”

In mid-June, Verlander was scheduled to return to the mound but suffered a left hamstring injury that Tigers manager A.J. Hinch said would sideline him for an extended period. According to the Tigers’ latest medical update, Verlander is “playing catch and completing rehab daily.”

Verlander, who is 266-159 over his career with a 3.33 ERA, is not yet back to throwing off the mound.
